decisions.choice: they: the people who had questioned the man, left unnamed
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. The nearest people in the story are the neighbors and those who had seen him begging, who asked how his eyes were opened and where Jesus was (9:8-12). John does not say who brought him or why.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees: here acting as the men with authority to judge the matter
alternatives: a formal session of the council
decisions.reason: The Pharisees were a movement devoted to studying the law of Moses and keeping it in detail, the Sabbath included. In John they act with the chief priests against Jesus (7:32, 45-48). Here they question the man and his parents and decide what to do about those who confess Jesus (9:22, 34). John does not say whether this was a formal court.

decisions.choice: the once blind: named by what he had been
decisions.reason: John identifies the man by his past: the one who was blind before. The phrase keeps the wonder of what has happened in view as the questioning begins.

decisions.choice: They bring (L); took (B, R)
decisions.reason: John tells this in the present tense, the historic present, as he often does; it happens again in 9:17 ("they say"). Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as English tells a story. This decision covers both verbs in the passage.

decisions.choice: Some people
decisions.reason: Readable gives the verb a subject, since a plain "they" has nothing to point back to at the start of a new scene. It does not say who they were (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (B) and the passé composé (R); Literal keeps John's present ("ils l’amènent", 9:13; "ils disent", 9:17) and uses the passé simple for his past tenses; speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for this passage (9:13-23). The passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, the past tense young readers know. Literal keeps the historic present where John uses it, as the English Literal does, and the imperfect where he shows talk going on ("disaient").

decisions.choice: On conduisit
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no named subject (meaning decision m1). French "on" says "people" without naming them, so Balanced needs no pronoun with nothing to refer to; Readable says "des gens", as the English says "some people".

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (Wanampeleka); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in the earlier chapters, for the whole of chapter 9.

decisions.choice: historic present: "dẫn" (also "nói" in 9:17) with no past marker
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs carry no tense, so the historic present shows at Literal only in the absence of "đã"; one decision for this passage.

decisions.choice: Historic present kept at Literal ("데려간다", "말한다" (9:17)); past tense at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Korean narrative can use the present for vividness, so Literal keeps John's tense; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary past. One decision per passage.

decisions.choice: Levam (L); levaram (B, R)
decisions.reason: John's historic present (also "dizem", 9:17) is kept at Literal; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the pretérito perfeito, as the English does. Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: "ይወስዱታል" (they bring him, L); "ወሰዱት" (they took him, B, R)

decisions.choice: "ዕውር" (blind, L, B); "ዓይነ ስውር" (R)

John often tells past events in the present tense (here and in 9:17). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as Hindi narrative does.

decisions.choice: "Ведут" (L); "привели" (B, R)

decisions.choice: a late remark that turns the story
decisions.reason: As in 5:9, John mentions the day only after the healing is told. The remark explains why the Pharisees take up the matter and sets up the dispute of verse 16.

decisions.choice: making mud: work forbidden on the Sabbath, as the Pharisees understood it
decisions.reason: God forbade Israel to do any work on the seventh day (Exodus 20:8-11). Later Jewish teaching, collected in the Mishnah about AD 200, lists kneading among the main kinds of work forbidden on the Sabbath (Shabbat 7:2); mixing earth and saliva into mud could count as kneading. John names the making of the mud, not only the healing, as the thing done on that day.

decisions.choice: opened his eyes: a healing where no life was in danger
decisions.reason: Later Jewish teaching allowed treatment on the Sabbath when a life was in danger (Mishnah Yoma 8:6). A man blind from birth was in no danger, so by that rule the healing could have waited a day. Jesus had already answered such a charge in 7:21-24.

decisions.choice: the mud: the wet earth Jesus made with his saliva
decisions.reason: The article points back to 9:6, where Jesus spat on the ground and made mud. The word means wet earth or clay; here it is a paste put on the man's eyes.

decisions.choice: it was on a Sabbath that (B); ... on a Sabbath (R)
alternatives: Now it was Sabbath on the day when (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the stress on the day with "it was on a Sabbath that"; Readable tells the deed first and ends on the day, which is what matters for the dispute.

decisions.choice: the weekly day of rest; the man's eyes
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word Sabbath, as at 5:9, and says whose eyes, since "his" right after Jesus could be misread.

decisions.choice: el día de descanso de cada semana
decisions.reason: As at 5:9: "sábado" is also the everyday name of the day, so Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: "ngày Sa-bát"
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliteration; Readable explains it once, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ለወሰ" (kneaded) for "made" the mud
decisions.reason: Amharic speaks of kneading mud or dough ("ለወሰ"); "ሠራ" would suggest building something. The point that this was work on the Sabbath stays clear.

decisions.choice: again ... also: the Pharisees ask what the neighbors had asked
alternatives: the Pharisees asked him a second time
decisions.reason: The neighbors had already asked how his eyes were opened (9:10). "Again" and "also" mark that the Pharisees now put the same question; they had not asked before in the story.

decisions.choice: received sight: came to see
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to look up or to see again. The man was born blind (9:1), so here it simply means to gain sight, as in 9:11 and 9:18.

decisions.choice: were asking: questioning, perhaps pressing him
decisions.reason: The verb is imperfect. It may simply set the scene of an exchange, or picture them pressing him with questions.

decisions.choice: in turn (B); now ... also (R)
decisions.reason: "Again" here means that the question is asked a second time in the story, not that the Pharisees repeat their own question (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable avoid a word that would suggest that.

decisions.choice: a su vez (B); también (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the question is asked a second time in the story (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "ዓይኑ በራ" (his eyes became light) for "received sight"

decisions.choice: a shorter account than in 9:11

decisions.choice: he: Jesus, not named
decisions.reason: The man does not name his healer here. The Pharisees know whom he means, and in verse 17 they ask about "him".

decisions.choice: I see: a present that lasts
decisions.reason: After two past actions the last verb is present: he sees now, and goes on seeing. The healing is not a passing moment.

decisions.choice: I can see now (B); now I can see (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "now" and "can" to bring out the present state after the past actions (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: He (plain, at the start of the quotation)
decisions.reason: The pronoun for Jesus starts the man's words, so it is capitalized either way and written plain.

decisions.choice: ahora
decisions.reason: As in English: brings out the present state (meaning decision m3). Spanish needs no pronoun for Jesus here.

decisions.choice: the healed man calls Jesus "ông ấy" and the Pharisees "các ông"; they call him "anh"
decisions.reason: He does not yet know who Jesus is (9:36), so he speaks of him as of a respected man; no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: The man answers the Pharisees in the formal style (합쇼체), calling himself "저"
alternatives: the plain style he used with his neighbours (9:9-12)
decisions.reason: The style guide's default to superiors. The Pharisees speak to him, and among themselves, in the plain style (해라체) and speak of Jesus without honorifics ("이 사람").

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; honorific "उन्होंने" for Jesus from the narrator, plain "उसने" from the healed man
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change; respect is shown by the honorific third person, as the style guide sets out. The healed man does not yet believe in Jesus (9:36-38), so he speaks of him plainly, as the Pharisees do ("यह", "उसने"). This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "Грязь положил он"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order with "грязь" first, which puts the pronoun for Jesus mid-sentence, so it takes the setting; at Balanced and Readable it starts the man's words and is written plain.

decisions.choice: the man speaks to the Pharisees in です・ます and calls Jesus "あの人"
decisions.reason: A beggar before the men who judge the matter speaks politely; he has not yet said what he thinks of Jesus, so he keeps the plain "あの人" of 9:11 until he calls him a prophet (9:17).

decisions.choice: from God: sent by God and acting with his authority
decisions.reason: To be "from God" is to come with God's commission. Nicodemus said that no one could do these signs unless God were with him (3:2), and the healed man will argue that if Jesus were not from God he could do nothing (9:33).

decisions.choice: their reasoning: one who breaks the Sabbath cannot be sent by God
decisions.reason: The law warned that a prophet who gave a sign and then led the people away from God's commands was not to be followed (Deuteronomy 13:1-5). These Pharisees start from the Sabbath: if Jesus broke it, whatever he did, he cannot come from God. Jesus had answered that charge before (5:17; 7:22-23).

decisions.choice: keep: observe, obey
decisions.reason: The verb means to keep or observe a command. The Pharisees judge Jesus by their own understanding of what the Sabbath forbids (meaning decision m2 at 9:14).

decisions.choice: this man: a distant, perhaps scornful way to speak of him
decisions.reason: They do not use Jesus's name but "this ... the man", with the words split for emphasis. It may carry a note of disdain, as in 5:12.

decisions.choice: two sentences, without "because"
alternatives: because he does not keep the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Readable gives the charge as its own sentence; the reason is still plain from the order.

decisions.choice: Il n’est pas de Dieu, cet homme-là
alternatives: Cet homme n’est pas de Dieu (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek splits "this ... the man" and puts the words apart for emphasis, perhaps with disdain (meaning decision m4). French shows the same by putting "cet homme-là" at the end, after the pronoun. Literal also says "garder" the Sabbath, the verb of "garder ma parole" (8:51); Balanced and Readable say "respecter", the everyday word.

decisions.choice: "người này", "ông ta" in the Pharisees' mouths, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The style guide's forms for opponents speaking of Jesus; "ông ta" keeps the distance the meaning decision notes in "this man".

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun alternatives, as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus and God is carried at every level by the subject honorific -si-, by "께서" and by "그분".

decisions.choice: "하나님께로부터 [온 자가] 아니다"
decisions.reason: Korean needs a verb with "from God"; Literal brackets the words it adds.

decisions.choice: não guarda o sábado, with no pronoun
decisions.reason: Portuguese leaves the subject unexpressed after "porque", so the pronoun the English puts under the deity_pronoun setting has no Portuguese word to carry it.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: "he" is in the verb ("አይጠብቅም", "አያከብርም")
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: "አይጠብቅም" (does not keep, L); "አያከብርም" (does not honour, observe, B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of keeping; "ሰንበትን ማክበር" is the usual Amharic for observing the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: "この男" (L, B), "あの男" (R)
decisions.reason: They speak of Jesus at a distance, perhaps with scorn, without his name (meaning decision m4); "男" carries that coolness in Japanese.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer: he cannot
decisions.reason: The question is not a request for information. It means that a sinner could not do such things. These Pharisees reason from the signs to the man, where the first group reasoned from the Sabbath to the man.

decisions.choice: a sinner: one who breaks God's law
decisions.reason: The word takes up the first group's charge: by breaking the Sabbath Jesus would be a sinner. The same word comes back in 9:24-25 and 9:31.

decisions.choice: such signs: deeds that point to God at work
decisions.reason: John calls Jesus's deeds signs (2:11; 4:54). A sign shows who the doer is; to these Pharisees the healing of a man born blind shows that God is with Jesus, as Nicodemus said in 3:2.

decisions.choice: others: other Pharisees
decisions.reason: "Others" stands against "some of the Pharisees" just before, and the next sentence says the division was "among them". These are Pharisees too.

decisions.choice: other Pharisees ... could not do signs like these!
alternatives: How is a man who is a sinner able to do such signs? (Literal)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects as a plain statement (meaning decision m1) and says who "others" were (meaning decision m4). Balanced keeps the question.

decisions.choice: otros fariseos ... no podría
decisions.reason: As in English: gives the answer the question expects (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "ምልክት" (sign), plural "ምልክቶች"
decisions.reason: John's word points beyond the deed (docs/john-terms.md): "ምልክት" keeps that, where "ተአምር" names only the wonder. Used for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "चिह्न" at every level
decisions.reason: Sign is a key term in John and is never "miracle": the word points beyond the deed, as the book's terms set out.

decisions.choice: "знамения" (L, B); "знаки" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John's word "sign": never "чудо", since the deed points beyond itself (docs/john-terms.md).

alignments.target_span: the man who had been blind

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, you of all people
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out, which in Greek gives it weight. Since the healing was done to him, the Pharisees, divided among themselves, ask for his view.

decisions.choice: since: giving the reason for asking
alternatives: that: "What do you say about him, that he opened your eyes?"
decisions.reason: The small word can give a reason ("since he opened your eyes") or state what they ask about ("what do you say about this, that he opened your eyes?"). The sense is close either way: they ask him to judge Jesus by what happened to him.

decisions.choice: the blind [man]: John still names him by what he had been
decisions.reason: John goes on calling him "the blind man" though he can now see, as in 9:13.

decisions.choice: the man who had been blind; And you (B); After all (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "who had been" so that "blind" is not misread as his present state, and "And you" carries the weight of the written-out pronoun (meaning decision m1). Readable puts the reason in its own sentence with "After all". Literal keeps the present "they say" (see the decision on the historic present at 9:13).

decisions.choice: tú, no setting
decisions.reason: The emphatic "tú" is the man himself and has no setting; "él" is Jesus.

decisions.choice: al que había sido ciego
decisions.reason: As in English: so that "ciego" is not misread as his present state.

decisions.choice: "その目の見えない[人]" (L); "目の見えなかったその人" (B); "あなた自身は" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's name for him, "the blind [man]" (meaning decision m3); Balanced says "見えなかった" so it is not read as his present state, and "あなた自身は" carries the written-out pronoun (m1).

decisions.choice: a prophet: a man sent by God to speak for him
decisions.reason: The word has no article: he says "a prophet", not "the Prophet" the crowd spoke of in 7:40. Prophets of Israel such as Elijah and Elisha were known for healings done by God's power (1 Kings 17:17-24; 2 Kings 5:1-14). The Samaritan woman came to the same view (4:19).

decisions.choice: a step in the man's growing understanding
decisions.reason: He first spoke of "the man called Jesus" (9:11); now he calls him a prophet; later he argues that Jesus is from God (9:33), and at last believes in him as the Son of Man and worships him (9:35-38).

decisions.choice: that: introduces his words
decisions.reason: The small word here simply opens a quotation, like quotation marks.

decisions.choice: The man
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, since the sentence that follows has another "he" for Jesus.

decisions.choice: a prophet, lowercase
decisions.reason: The capital is kept for the expected figure of 1:21 and 7:40; here the man means a prophet like those of old (meaning decision m1). "He" for Jesus starts the quotation, so it is written plain.

decisions.choice: un profeta, lower case
decisions.reason: As in English: a prophet like those of old, not the expected Prophet of 1:21 and 7:40 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "그분은 예언자이십니다": the man now speaks of Jesus with the honorific
decisions.reason: In 9:11 and 9:15 he spoke of "the man called Jesus" without honorifics. Calling him a prophet, a man sent by God, he now uses "그분" and "-이시-", and keeps them from here on (9:25-38): Korean lets his growing faith be heard in his grammar.

decisions.choice: "예언자" for prophētēs
decisions.reason: As through the book (docs/korean-style.md): "예언자" is the current word that new readers understand; "선지자" is the established older Protestant term, and a reviewer may prefer it for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "भविष्यद्वक्ता" (L, B); "नबी" (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's word for prophet; Readable uses the everyday "नबी".

decisions.choice: "あの方" (from here on in the man's speech)
decisions.reason: Calling Jesus a prophet is a step in the man's growing understanding (meaning decision m2); the change from "あの人" to the respectful "あの方" lets Japanese show the step.

fr.B: Les chefs juifs ne crurent pas qu’il avait été aveugle et qu’il avait reçu la vue, jusqu’à ce qu’ils aient convoqué les parents de l’homme qui voyait maintenant. \v 19 Ils leur demandèrent : « Est-ce bien votre fils, celui dont vous dites qu’il est né aveugle ?
fr.R: Les chefs juifs ne voulaient pas croire que l’homme avait été aveugle et qu’il voyait maintenant. Ils ont donc fait venir ses parents. \v 19 Ils leur ont demandé : « Est-ce que c’est votre fils ? Vous dites qu’il est né aveugle ?

sw.B: Viongozi wa Wayahudi hawakuamini kwamba alikuwa kipofu na amepata kuona, mpaka walipowaita wazazi wa mtu yule aliyeweza kuona sasa. \v 19 Wakawauliza, "Je, huyu ni mwana wenu, yule mnayesema alizaliwa kipofu?

vi.L: Vậy những người Do Thái không tin về anh ta rằng anh ta đã bị mù và được sáng mắt, cho đến khi họ gọi cha mẹ của người được sáng mắt ấy đến, \v 19 và hỏi họ rằng: "Đây có phải là con trai của ông bà, mà ông bà nói là sinh ra đã bị mù không?
vi.B: Các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái không tin rằng anh ta đã bị mù và nay được sáng mắt, cho đến khi họ cho gọi cha mẹ của người được sáng mắt ấy đến. \v 19 Họ hỏi: "Đây có phải là con trai ông bà, người mà ông bà nói là sinh ra đã bị mù không?
vi.R: Các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái không chịu tin rằng người ấy đã bị mù mà nay thấy được, cho đến khi họ cho gọi cha mẹ anh ta đến. \v 19 Họ hỏi: "Đây có phải là con trai ông bà không? Ông bà nói anh ta sinh ra đã bị mù sao?

ko.L: 그러므로 유대인들은, 보게 된 그 사람의 부모를 불러오기까지는, 그에 관하여 그가 눈멀었다가 보게 되었다는 것을 믿지 않았다. \v 19 그리고 그들에게 물으며 말했다. "이 사람이, 너희가 눈먼 채로 태어났다고 말하는, 너희 아들이냐?

ko.R: 유대 지도자들은 그 사람의 부모를 불러오기 전까지는, 그가 눈멀었다가 이제 보게 되었다는 것을 믿으려 하지 않았다. \v 19 그들이 부모에게 물었다. "이 사람이 너희 아들이냐? 너희는 이 아들이 태어날 때부터 앞을 보지 못했다고 말하는 것이냐?

hi.L: पर यहूदियों ने उसके विषय में विश्वास नहीं किया कि वह अंधा था और उसने दृष्टि पाई, जब तक उन्होंने उस दृष्टि पानेवाले के माता-पिता को न बुलाया, \v 19 और उनसे यह कहते हुए पूछा, "क्या यह तुम्हारा पुत्र है, जिसके विषय में तुम कहते हो कि यह अंधा जन्मा था?

hi.R: यहूदी अगुवे इस बात पर विश्वास करने को तैयार नहीं थे कि वह आदमी अंधा था और अब देख सकता है, जब तक कि उन्होंने उसके माता-पिता को नहीं बुलवा लिया। \v 19 उन्होंने उनसे पूछा, "क्या यह तुम्हारा बेटा है? क्या तुम कहते हो कि यह अंधा पैदा हुआ था?

ru.B: Иудейские власти не поверили, что он был слепым и прозрел, пока не вызвали родителей прозревшего. \v 19 Они спросили их: «Это ваш сын, о котором вы говорите, что он родился слепым?

uk.B: Юдейська влада не вірила, що він був сліпий і прозрів, доки не покликали батьків чоловіка, який тепер бачив. \v 19 Вони запитали їх: «Це ваш син, той, про якого ви кажете, що він народився сліпим?

ja.B: ユダヤ人の指導者たちは、その人が目が見えなかったのに見えるようになったことを、見えるようになったその人の両親を呼び出すまでは信じなかった。\v 19 彼らは両親に尋ねた。「これは、生まれつき目が見えなかったとあなたがたが言っている、あなたがたの息子か？

decisions.choice: the Jews: the same Pharisees and authorities as in verses 13-17
alternatives: a different group from the Pharisees
decisions.reason: John switches from "the Pharisees" to "the Jews" without a break in the story. The people meant are those who have been questioning the man and who will question his parents, in other words the authorities. It is not the people as a whole: the man and his parents are Jews too, and so is Jesus.

decisions.choice: until: their disbelief held until the parents were called
decisions.reason: They refused to accept the healing as fact and looked for witnesses. Parents could say who their son was and whether he had been blind from birth, which no one else could prove.

decisions.choice: you say: emphatic, putting the claim on them
decisions.reason: The "you" is written out: "whom you say". The question treats the blindness from birth as the parents' claim, as if it might be false, and so presses them to answer for it.

decisions.choice: the one who had received sight: John keeps the healing in view
decisions.reason: Even as he tells of their disbelief, John names the man by what has happened to him. The words added after "his parents" stress the point.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: summoned the parents of the man who could now see (B); called for his parents (R)
alternatives: called his parents, [the parents] of the one who had received sight (Literal)
decisions.reason: The Greek names the parents twice over ("his parents, of the one who had received sight"); Balanced folds the two into one phrase, and Readable keeps only "his parents". Readable splits the question in two.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the same Pharisees and authorities who are questioning the man (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les chefs juifs (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John. Literal keeps the word John wrote. Here it means the authorities who have been questioning the man (meaning decision m1), and in French "les Juifs" alone would read as the whole people, to which the man, his parents and Jesus belong; Balanced and Readable name the group. The same holds in verse 22.

decisions.choice: Ils ont donc fait venir ses parents.
alternatives: jusqu’à ce qu’ils aient fait venir ses parents
decisions.reason: Readable makes the long "until" clause a sentence of its own; the order of events and the reason for calling the parents (meaning decision m2) stay the same.

decisions.choice: Wayahudi (L); viongozi wa Wayahudi (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the earlier chapters: here the Pharisees and authorities are meant, so Balanced and Readable name the leaders. The same in verses 22 and 24.

decisions.choice: "những người Do Thái" (L); "các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rule for the Jews where the authorities are meant (9:18, 9:22).

decisions.choice: the authorities call the parents "ông bà"
decisions.reason: Polite but official; "các người" would sound rude to elderly parents in modern Vietnamese.

decisions.choice: "유대인들" (L); "유대 지도자들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here, as the meaning decision says, the authorities are meant (the Pharisees of 9:13-17). The book-wide Korean choice names them at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps the word John wrote. This holds for 9:22.

decisions.choice: os líderes judeus (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the book's terms: where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them, here and in 9:22; Literal keeps "os judeus", the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: "አይሁድ" (the Jews, L); "የአይሁድ መሪዎች" (the Jewish leaders, B, R)
decisions.reason: As docs/john-terms.md: Literal keeps the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the authorities, as the meaning decision reads it. Used for the whole passage (also 9:22).

decisions.choice: "यहूदी" (L); "यहूदी अगुवे" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the authorities (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the leaders, as the book's terms set out. The man and his parents are Jews too.

decisions.choice: "иудеи" (L); "иудейские власти" (B); "иудейские вожди" (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the authorities, the same Pharisees as in 9:13-17 (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the leaders, as the book's terms require. The man, his parents and Jesus are all Jews.

decisions.choice: "юдейська влада" (B), "юдейські провідники" (R)
decisions.reason: The Jews here are the Pharisees and authorities of 9:13-17 (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps "юдеї", the other levels name the authorities, as in 9:22. The man and his parents are Jews too.

decisions.choice: "ユダヤ人たち" (L); "ユダヤ人の指導者たち" (B, R)
alternatives: "ユダヤ人たち" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the word means the authorities who have been questioning the man (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable name them, as the book's terms say. The man, his parents and Jesus are Jews too.

decisions.choice: he is of age: he is an adult, old enough to answer for himself
decisions.reason: The phrase means to have reached full age. As an adult the man could be questioned in his own right and give his own testimony; his parents need not answer for him. Later Jewish teaching counted a boy responsible for keeping the commandments from age thirteen (Mishnah Avot 5:21); the man here is plainly a grown man.

decisions.choice: we ... him ... he himself: the parents hand the questions back to their son
decisions.reason: "We" is written out in the second "we do not know", "him" comes first in "ask him", and "he" and "himself" are stressed in the last clause. Each word pushes responsibility away from the parents and onto the son.

decisions.choice: who opened his eyes: they say they do not know
decisions.reason: The parents claim not to know who healed him. Verse 22 explains why they speak so carefully; John does not say whether they knew or had heard the name of Jesus.

decisions.choice: of age and can answer for himself (B); He is a grown man. He can speak for himself. (R)
alternatives: He is of age; he will speak for himself (Literal)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "of age" means (meaning decision m1). "Can" at Balanced and Readable brings out that he is able to answer, which is the point of the parents' remark.

decisions.choice: mayor de edad (B); un hombre adulto (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: says what "of age" means (meaning decision m1). "Él" and "sí mismo" are the son and have no setting.

decisions.choice: il a l’âge [requis] (L); il est majeur (B); c’est un adulte (R)
alternatives: il est en âge de répondre
decisions.reason: The Greek "he has age" means he is an adult who can answer for himself (meaning decision m1). French "il a l’âge" needs a complement, which Literal brackets; "il a de l’âge" would mean he is old. Balanced uses "majeur", the everyday word for someone legally of age; Readable says "un adulte". The same words return in verse 23.

decisions.choice: ele tem idade (L); é maior de idade (B); é adulto (R)
decisions.reason: "Maior de idade" is the plain Brazilian legal phrase for an adult who answers for himself (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps the bare "ter idade". "É de maior" is spoken, not written.

decisions.choice: "ዕድሜው ደርሷል" (his age has come, L, B); "ትልቅ ሰው ነው" (he is a grown man, R)
decisions.reason: The Amharic idiom for coming of age; Readable says it in the plainest words.

decisions.choice: "पूछिए": the parents say "आप" to the authorities
decisions.reason: Ordinary people address those in authority with "आप", as the style guide sets out; the leaders say "तुम" to the parents and to their son.

decisions.choice: "बालिग़ है" (L, B); "अब बड़ा हो चुका है" (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom means he is an adult, old enough to answer for himself (meaning decision m1); "बालिग़" says that, and Readable puts it in everyday words. The same in 9:23.

records.literal_gloss: These things said the parents of him because they were fearing the Jews, already for had agreed the Jews that if anyone him confessed Christ, out-of-the-synagogue he would become.

en.L: His parents said these things because they were afraid of the Jews, for the Jews had already agreed that if anyone confessed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [to be the] {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, {{gender:they|he}} would be put out of the synagogue.

vi.R: Cha mẹ anh ta trả lời như vậy vì họ sợ các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái. Các nhà lãnh đạo ấy đã thỏa thuận với nhau rằng nếu ai công khai nói Đức Giê-xu là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, thì người đó sẽ bị đuổi ra khỏi nhà hội.

ko.L: 그의 부모가 이렇게 말한 것은 유대인들을 두려워했기 때문이다. 유대인들이 이미, 누구든지 그분을 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}로 고백하면 회당에서 쫓겨나게 하기로 합의해 두었던 것이다.
ko.B: 그의 부모가 이렇게 말한 것은 유대 지도자들이 두려웠기 때문이다. 그들은 이미, 누구든지 그분을 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}로 고백하는 사람은 회당에서 내쫓기로 결정해 두었다.
ko.R: 그의 부모가 이렇게 대답한 것은 유대 지도자들이 무서웠기 때문이다. 지도자들은 누구든지 예수를 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}라고 드러내 놓고 말하면 그 사람을 회당에서 쫓아내기로 이미 뜻을 모아 두었다.

pt.L: Os pais dele disseram essas coisas porque tinham medo dos judeus, pois os judeus já tinham combinado que, se alguém {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} confessasse [como o] {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}, seria expulso da sinagoga.
pt.B: Os pais dele falaram assim por medo dos líderes judeus, que já tinham decidido que quem {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} confessasse como o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}} seria expulso da sinagoga.
pt.R: Os pais dele responderam assim porque tinham medo dos líderes judeus. Esses líderes já tinham combinado entre si que, se alguém dissesse abertamente que Jesus era o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}, essa pessoa seria expulsa da sinagoga.

am.L: ወላጆቹ ይህን ያሉት አይሁድን ስለ ፈሩ ነው፤ ማንም እርሱን {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} [ነው ብሎ] ቢመሰክር ከምኩራብ እንዲወገድ አይሁድ አስቀድመው ተስማምተው ነበርና።

am.R: ወላጆቹ እንዲህ ብለው የመለሱት የአይሁድን መሪዎች ስለ ፈሩ ነው። መሪዎቹ ኢየሱስን {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ነው ብሎ በግልጽ የሚናገር ሰው ሁሉ ከምኩራብ እንዲባረር አስቀድመው ተስማምተው ነበር።

ru.L: Это сказали родители его, потому что боялись иудеев, ведь иудеи уже договорились, что если кто признает {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} {{christos:Христом|Мессией}}, тот будет отлучён от синагоги.
ru.B: Его родители говорили так из страха перед иудейскими властями, которые уже договорились, что всякого, кто признает {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} {{christos:Христом|Мессией}}, отлучат от синагоги.
ru.R: Его родители ответили так, потому что боялись иудейских вождей. Вожди уже договорились между собой, что если кто-то открыто скажет, что Иисус — {{christos:Христос|Мессия}}, того выгонят из синагоги.

uk.L: Це сказали його батьки, бо боялися юдеїв, бо юдеї вже домовилися, що коли хтось визнає {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} {{christos:Христом|Месією}}, той буде відлучений від синагоги.
uk.B: Його батьки говорили так, бо боялися юдейської влади, яка вже ухвалила, що кожного, хто визнає {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} {{christos:Христом|Месією}}, відлучать від синагоги.
uk.R: Його батьки відповіли так, бо боялися юдейських провідників. Ці провідники вже домовилися між собою, що коли хтось відкрито скаже, що Ісус — {{christos:Христос|Месія}}, ту людину виженуть із синагоги.

ja.L: 彼の両親がこう言ったのは、ユダヤ人たちを恐れていたからである。ユダヤ人たちは、もしだれかがイエスを{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}[である]と告白するなら、その者は会堂から追放されると、すでに取り決めていたのである。
ja.B: 両親がこのように話したのは、ユダヤ人の指導者たちを恐れていたからである。指導者たちは、イエスを{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}であると告白する者があれば、会堂から追放すると、すでに申し合わせていた。
ja.R: 両親がこう答えたのは、ユダヤ人の指導者たちを恐れていたからです。指導者たちは、イエスが{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}だとはっきり言う人がいれば、その人を会堂から追い出すことに、もう決めていたのです。

decisions.choice: the Jews (twice): the authorities
decisions.reason: Both times the word means the leaders who were questioning the man, the same group called Pharisees in verses 13-16. It cannot mean the people as a whole: the parents who fear them are Jews themselves, and so are the man and Jesus. Those who "agreed" on a penalty are men with power over the synagogue.

decisions.choice: put out of the synagogue: shut out of the community's worship and common life
alternatives: a formal, written ban in force across the land
no more than an informal threat
decisions.reason: The word (ἀποσυνάγωγος) is found in the New Testament only in John (9:22; 12:42; 16:2). The synagogue was where Jews met each Sabbath for prayer and the reading of Scripture, and it was also the center of the town's shared life, so to be put out of it was to be cut off from one's people. Later Jewish sources speak of synagogue discipline that shut a person out for a time. No source outside John records a measure in Jesus's lifetime against those who confessed him; the verse speaks of an agreement among the leaders, and how formal it was and how far it reached is not known.

decisions.choice: confess: say openly, acknowledge in public
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare openly what one holds to be true. John the Baptist "confessed" that he was not the Christ (1:20); in 12:42 some rulers believed in Jesus but would not confess it for fear of being put out of the synagogue.

decisions.choice: had already agreed: a decision taken before this hearing
decisions.reason: The verb is in a past-before-past tense with "already": the leaders had agreed on the penalty before the parents were called. People were afraid to speak openly about Jesus for fear of these authorities as early as 7:13.

decisions.choice: him ... Christ: confessing that he is the Christ
decisions.reason: "Christ" here has no article in Greek; it states what the person would confess Jesus to be. It is the title, the anointed king Israel was waiting for (1:41; 7:41), not a name.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: [to be the] {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); as the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (B); was the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (R); {{gender:they|he}} (L)
decisions.reason: "Christ" is the title (meaning decision m5), so every level writes "the" before the setting, Literal in brackets because the Greek has no article. "Anyone" means a man or a woman, so the pronoun after it in Literal carries the gender setting; Balanced says "anyone who" and Readable "that person", which need none. Balanced joins the two mentions of the leaders with "who".

decisions.choice: openly said Jesus was
decisions.reason: Readable explains "confess" (meaning decision m3) and names Jesus for "him", since the nearest "him" is the parents' son.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the same Pharisees and authorities who are questioning the man (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

decisions.choice: [como el] Cristo (L); como el Cristo (B); era el Cristo (R)
decisions.reason: "Cristo" is the title here (meaning decision m5), so every level writes "el" before the setting, Literal in brackets. "Alguien" needs no gender setting in Spanish.

decisions.choice: [comme le] {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (L); comme le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (B); était le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (R); no gender setting on "il" (L)
decisions.reason: "Christ" is the title here (meaning decision m5), so every level writes "le" before the span, Literal in brackets with "comme" because the Greek has neither. As in 8:51, "il" after "quelqu’un" is the grammatical agreement and reads as anyone, so French has no gender span where the English has "they/he"; Readable says "cette personne".

decisions.choice: confessait (L); reconnaîtrait (B); disait ouvertement (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to declare openly what one holds true (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "confesser", the word French uses for confessing one's faith; Balanced uses the plainer "reconnaître comme"; Readable says it in everyday words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: atatengwa na sinagogi
decisions.reason: ἀποσυνάγωγος means being shut out of the synagogue community, not only out of a building, as the meaning note says. "Kutengwa na" (to be cut off from) says that; Readable uses the plainer "kufukuzwa kutoka" (thrown out of). No gender span is needed for "mtu yeyote" (anyone).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}; "người ấy" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Đấng" makes Christ a title, as "the" does in English. "Người ấy" is already inclusive, so the gender setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: "nhà hội" for synagogue
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant word; "hội đường" is the Catholic one.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "누구든지 ... 쫓겨나게"
alternatives: "그 사람" with a gender span, as in the English "they|he"
decisions.reason: Korean "누구든지" (anyone) needs no following pronoun and is already inclusive, so the gender setting has nothing to change. The christos span follows the style guide.

decisions.choice: se alguém ..., seria expulso, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Portuguese leaves the subject of "seria expulso" unexpressed, so "alguém" covers men and women and needs no setting; the masculine participle is the ordinary generic form.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "ማንም ... ቢመሰክር" (anyone ... confesses)
decisions.reason: Amharic "ማንም" with the generic masculine verb already includes women and men, so there are not two wordings to choose between. Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: "यहूदी" (L); "यहूदी अगुवे" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Both times the word means the authorities (meaning decision m1), as in 9:18; the parents themselves are Jews.

decisions.choice: "मसीह", with no christos span
decisions.reason: "मसीह" is both the familiar title and the word Messiah itself, so the choice the English setting offers is already made; the style guide gives Hindi no christos setting. Hindi needs no article for the title to be read as one.

decisions.choice: "कोई ... वह", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Hindi "वह" means he or she alike, so there is nothing for the gender setting to change.

decisions.choice: "иудеев ... иудеи" (L); "иудейскими властями" (B); "иудейских вождей" (R)
decisions.reason: Both times the word means the authorities (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the leaders. The parents themselves are Jews.

decisions.choice: "признает его Христом / Мессией", the christos setting inflected in each option; "кто ..., тот" with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Russian puts the title in the instrumental with no article or supplied words, so Literal needs no bracket. The English has a gender setting on "they / he"; Russian "кто ..., тот" is already inclusive, so it has none.

decisions.choice: "хтось ..., той" with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Ukrainian "хтось ..., той" already covers men and women, so the English gender setting has no Ukrainian span here.

decisions.choice: "відлучений від синагоги" (L, B), "виженуть із синагоги" (R)
decisions.reason: Being shut out of the synagogue's worship and common life (meaning decision m2); "відлучити" is the established word for such exclusion, Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: {{christos:キリスト|メシア}}[である]と (L); "その者", "その人" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Christ is the title here (meaning decision m5), so it takes the setting with "である", which Literal brackets. The English needs a gender span for the pronoun after "anyone"; Japanese "その者" and "その人" are already inclusive. Both mentions of "the Jews" mean the authorities (m1).

decisions.choice: the parents' words repeated in reverse order
decisions.reason: In verse 21 they said "Ask him; he is of age"; John now quotes the words the other way round. The repetition closes the explanation that began in verse 22 and returns to the story.

decisions.choice: ask: the same request as in verse 21
decisions.reason: The verb here has a prefix the one in verse 21 lacks, but the sense is the same: question him.

decisions.choice: Question him (B); a grown man (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "question" for the longer verb (meaning decision m2). As in verse 21, Readable says plainly what "of age" means.

decisions.choice: Interróguenlo (B)
decisions.reason: As in English: a stronger word for the longer verb (meaning decision m2).
